## On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Status:** Ongoing / unresolved (last log line at 03:59:27Z still failing, backlog growing)

**Impact window:** 2026-03-14 02:14:18Z → ongoing as of 03:59:27Z (last timestamp in `logs/gateway.log`). Traffic was clean before 02:14; no self-recovery observed — queued waiters grew from 13 to 74+ over the window.

**Root cause:** `gateway.pool.perRequest` was flipped `false -> true` in config generation 119, applied at 02:13:41Z. This made the gateway acquire a new connection per request instead of reusing pooled ones, exhausting the fixed 20-connection pool almost immediately under normal load. First `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED` / 503 fired at 02:14:18.972Z, ~30s after the config took effect. Every upstream (billing-svc, orders-svc, catalog-svc, accounts-svc) is affected identically, confirming it's the gateway's own pool, not a backend outage.

**Deploy to roll back:** `dep-4471` — service `gateway`, author **a.novak**, 2026-03-14T02:12:00Z–02:14:00Z, "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation." This is the only deploy in `deploys.csv` that lines up with the incident onset (nearest others: dep-4470 worker finished 77 min earlier; dep-4472 billing-svc didn't start until 02:41Z).

**Scope:** Gateway only. `worker.log` shows zero errors across the same window — job processing (email/webhook/settle/export/cleanup/reindex) continued normally with unaffected `db_wait` times, confirming workers use a separate pool and were not impacted.

**Recommended action:** Roll back dep-4471 (or set `gateway.pool.perRequest` back to `false`) and redeploy. No workaround needed on the worker fleet.
